statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and the four slots up to the scheduled 22:00Z reopen contain no tradable Nasdaq-100 interval at all; the twenty slots from the reopen onward carry conditional Tail readings between 10 and 18, every one of them below the block threshold. Stress is 42, moderate, and higher than the previous hour because Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary has now publicly threatened Gulf and Hormuz oil flows outright, adding to a reported Monday US Treasury briefing on the toughest sanctions package yet, Brent at 94.39 dollars after a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%, and long-end yields that gave back Friday's buyback relief. None of it can be priced until the venue reopens. Confidence is 84, high, on index levels verified at the index owner plus H.15 yields, oil, volatility, verified geopolitical primary sources and a checked calendar, limited only by the absence of a live price path.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: the Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day yet below its own open, while the VIX settled at 14.89 after a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced, so no persistent directional efficiency is on record and nothing in the current evidence set establishes one. The new element this hour is rhetorical rather than structural, and rhetoric that has not yet reached a price cannot be scored as path evidence. Tail-relevant structure cannot be observed again until the 22:00Z reopen, so the narrow evidence-based danger window covers 22:00Z to 02:00Z, when the weekend information set is repriced into thin liquidity. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Closed-venue assessment four hours before the reopen: Tail holds the floor of 4 through the remaining shut hours, then carries conditional readings between 10 and 18 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen through Monday's US cash session, while an explicit Iranian threat to Gulf and Hormuz oil flows, a reported Monday US sanctions briefing and Brent above 94 dollars all wait for a venue in which to be priced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T18:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T17:00:00Z, so four closed hours are followed by the reopen slot and nineteen tradable hours, and Monday's 12:30Z Chicago Fed release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 15:30Z bill auctions all fall inside the window. The Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, having opened at 29,359.60 and traded a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range; this level is confirmed directly at the index owner, whose page carries the same high, low and net change. One widely used quote page returned a materially different level for the same instrument during this run and was discarded in favour of the index owner. Both extremes were retraced and the index finished below its own open, which is mean-reverting rather than one-way behaviour. The broader tape agreed on the day: S&P 500 +0.43% at 7,674.37, Nasdaq Composite +0.43% at 26,180.46 and the Dow +0.98% at 53,277.01, even though all three finished the week lower, the Nasdaq Composite by 2.0%. The VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0%, which is not a stressed volatility print. The most recent H.15 constant maturity yields are 4.19% at two years, 4.69% at ten years and 5.23% at thirty years, and Friday's reporting has the long end giving back the relief that followed the expanded Treasury buyback announcement, with the 30-year quoted back near 5.27% and the 10-year near 4.73%. Brent is 94.39 dollars and WTI 87.06 dollars after a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%. The change since the previous hour is geopolitical: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary stated that not a single drop of oil will leave the Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz if neighbouring states join the US economic campaign, and warned that such states would be treated as enemies, while Iran's central bank governor described Iranian oil exports as having fallen to zero. The US Treasury secretary is reported to be detailing the sanctions package at a news conference on Monday; because no exact time has been published, that briefing is deliberately left out of the event calendar and carried instead as a diffuse timing risk inside Monday's forecast hours. Shared cross-asset context collected at 18:01Z is delayed, latest-session material and is used only as confirmation: it shows Friday's futures direction modestly positive across NQ, ES and YM with VIX futures lower, gold up 2.39% and Treasury futures lower across the curve, megacaps split five to three with a 1.8 point dispersion, and semiconductors averaging about -0.7% against software groups above 1%. That is a mixed internal picture, which reduces directional conviction rather than establishing the aligned one-way structure that a higher Tail would require. Applying the standing method, event importance, headline severity and forecast dispersion raise Stress and shape Confidence; only observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension and index levels holding near session extremes raise Tail. None of those can exist while the venue is shut, and none were present in the last observed session. Tail therefore stays at the closed-venue floor of 4 for the current hour, and the conditional path peaks at 18 in Monday's first full cash hour, ten points below the level at which new base entries would be blocked.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 19 hourly assessments are available and 5 clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable (21:00Z on 22 August, 07:00Z on 23 August, 10:00Z on 23 August, 11:00Z on 23 August, 12:00Z on 23 August). Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress traced a shut-weekend arc, easing from 41 at the start of the window to a low of 34 in the European morning before turning higher through the afternoon to 40 in the most recent published hour as the reopen drew closer. Confidence eased from 87 to 85 as the last observed session receded further into the past.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The next three slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress climbs from 42 to 45 as the reopen approaches with a heavier unpriced queue than at the previous assessment. The final twenty slots are tradable. The 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 14 and the first full hour after it 15, on the untested assumption that a weekend gap could extend before retracing; an orderly two-way reopen would invalidate that. Conditional Tail then decays to 10 through the quiet Asian hours, where two-way trade has historically been most reliable, before rebuilding through the European session to 14 into the 12:30Z Chicago Fed release, 17 at the 13:30Z US cash open and a horizon peak of 18 in the first full cash hour. Even that peak sits ten points below the block threshold, because the alignment that would justify more is hypothetical at assessment time rather than observed. The Monday sanctions briefing has no published time, so it is treated as diffuse timing risk across the US hours instead of a dated calendar event.
